support_ticket_routing::contradictions::.text: {"contradictions":[{"id":"C1","topic":"Current routing accuracy: 78% in the FY26 objectives vs 71% in the metrics series","kind":"metric_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-68cdd2b1","quote":"Routing accuracy sits at 78%.","locator":"support_objectives.md, Current position"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-ac5740e1","quote":"value: 71.2","locator":"routing_metrics.csv row 5, period 2026-Q1, metric routing_accuracy_queue_level"},"summary":"The strategy document's headline accuracy figure (78%) is stale and belongs to a retired definition and an older period: it matches the 2025-Q1 department-level row, not the current queue-level series, which reads 71.2% for 2026-Q1 and 71.4% for 2026-Q2. Support analytics states explicitly that the 78% figure still circulating in planning documents is the 2025-Q1 department-level number (EV-3e2d12e8: \"The 78% figure that still circulates in planning documents is the 2025-Q1 department-level number\").","how_to_resolve":"Have product-leadership restate the FY26 baseline using the queue-level metric name from routing_metrics.csv and the period it was measured in (2026-Q1 = 71.2%, 2026-Q2 = 71.4%), and mark the 78% figure as 2025-Q1 department-level."},{"id":"C2","topic":"Whether pre- and post-April-2025 routing accuracy figures are comparable","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-db957a15","quote":"note: definition retired 2025-04-01 - department level - not comparable with queue level figures - synthetic","locator":"routing_metrics.csv row 1, period 2025-Q1"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-3e2d12e8","quote":"Under the old definition a ticket counted as correctly routed if it reached the correct department, of which there were three. Under the current definition it counts as correctly routed only if it reached the correct queue, of which there are five.","locator":"data_tooling_notes.md, Routing accuracy definition change"},"summary":"Both records describe the same fact from different sides: the 78.2% figure measures a three-department taxonomy, the 71.x% figures measure a five-queue taxonomy. Any narrative of accuracy 'falling from 78% to 71%' is comparing two different populations of routing decisions, not a regression.","how_to_resolve":"Restate any trend line using only routing_accuracy_queue_level rows (2025-Q2 onward). If a pre-2025-Q2 queue-level number is needed, ask support-analytics whether historical tickets can be re-scored under the five-queue definition."},{"id":"C3","topic":"Median time-to-resolution baseline: 21 hours vs 22.0 / 22.6 hours","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-68cdd2b1","quote":"Reduce median time-to-resolution for customer support tickets from 21 hours to 12 hours by the end of FY26.","locator":"support_objectives.md, Annual goals (document updated 2026-01-20)"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-133fecfa","quote":"value: 22.6","locator":"routing_metrics.csv row 11, period 2026-Q2, metric median_time_to_resolution_hours"},"summary":"The '21 hours' baseline in the objectives corresponds to the 2025-Q4 reading (EV-ff35851f: \"value: 21.2\"), the latest available when the document was written in January 2026. The series has since moved the other way: 22.0 hours in 2026-Q1 and 22.6 hours in 2026-Q2. Both figures are true of their own quarter; the goal gap is now 10.6 hours, not 9.","how_to_resolve":"Re-baseline the FY26 goal against the most recent quarter in routing_metrics.csv and state the period alongside the number."},{"id":"C4","topic":"Whether reported median time-to-resolution measures how long customers actually waited","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-428cdc6c","quote":"value: 22.0","locator":"routing_metrics.csv row 10, period 2026-Q1, metric median_time_to_resolution_hours"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-3e2d12e8","quote":"A reopened issue contributes two resolution times, each shorter than the elapsed time the customer actually waited.","locator":"data_tooling_notes.md, Reopen behaviour in the volume export"},"summary":"The headline time-to-resolution metric is computed per record, and since the Relay 5.2 release each reopened issue produces two records. With 14% of 2026-Q2 tickets reopened within 14 days (EV-71c6137f: \"value: 14.0\"), the published median understates customer-experienced wait by an unquantified amount, so the metric the goal is written against and the quantity the goal cares about are not the same thing.","how_to_resolve":"Ask support-analytics to produce a per-issue time-to-resolution that stitches clone records back to their `reopened_from` original, and compare it with the per-record series for 2025-Q4 through 2026-Q2."},{"id":"C5","topic":"Year-over-year ticket volume growth of 16.7%","kind":"metric_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-68cdd2b1","quote":"Ticket volume is up 16.7% year over year, from 35,900 to 41,880 per quarter.","locator":"support_objectives.md, Current position"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-3e2d12e8","quote":"A year-over-year comparison that uses `exported_rows` across that date is comparing two different things and will overstate growth.","locator":"data_tooling_notes.md, Reopen behaviour in the volume export"},"summary":"The 16.7% figure compares 2025-Q2 exported_rows (35,900, with zero reopen clones per EV-00512857) against 2026-Q2 exported_rows (41,880, of which 5,140 are clones per EV-e8b9716e). On the distinct-issue basis the tooling notes prescribe, 2026-Q2 is 36,740 issues, roughly 2% above 2025-Q2. Delia Okonjo's meeting statement repeats the inflated figure (EV-6404931e: \"Volume is up nearly 17% and we are holding headcount.\").","how_to_resolve":"Recompute the year-over-year comparison as exported_rows minus reopen_rows_included for both quarters, and answer the question raised and not answered in the review: how much of the increase is reopened tickets rather than new ones."},{"id":"C6","topic":"Whether further rules-engine tuning can raise accuracy","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-6404931e","quote":"We have not really invested in the rules engine. Two more tuning passes and we would be at 85%.","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Marek Vandal, Head of Support"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-79d2ae90","quote":"Our assessment is that keyword rules have reached their ceiling on this ticket mix.","locator":"routing_engine_history.md, Assessment 2026-06-30"},"summary":"The Head of Support expects roughly +14 points from two more tuning passes; support-engineering's version log shows three expansion passes adding 176 rules moved accuracy 0.6 points in twelve months and expects no different from a fourth. Marek named no specific passes (EV-6404931e records that \"he said the team would work it out\").","how_to_resolve":"Ask Marek for the specific rule families he believes are missing, and have support-engineering score them against the 2026-Q1 held-out set; the rules engine can be replayed offline, as the classifier trial did."},{"id":"C7","topic":"Does adding a model require new ML infrastructure spend in FY26","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-68cdd2b1","quote":"standing up dedicated model-serving infrastructure for support was quoted at $180k of capital plus two engineers","locator":"support_objectives.md, D-2025-11 (dated 2025-11-14)"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-ac98dec8","quote":"Adding a third model requires no new infrastructure and no new vendor.","locator":"technical_constraints.md, Model serving"},"summary":"Both were true when written. The FY26 no-ML-spend decision was taken 2025-11-14, before the internal serving platform existed; Modelyard went live 2026-02-09, hosts CPU inference up to 2 GB, and already carries two fulfilment models. The 340 MB trial model with 41 ms median inference fits inside both that limit and the platform's 400 ms routing budget, so the cost premise behind D-2025-11 may no longer hold — but the decision itself has not been revisited in evidence.","how_to_resolve":"Have engineering-leadership re-examine D-2025-11 against the Modelyard cost position, and have data-platform close the trial's open gap: \"We have not estimated the cost of running or retraining this model in production.\""},{"id":"C8","topic":"Does the classifier beat the rules engine — overall vs per queue","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"Overall the classifier routed 88.5% of held-out tickets to the correct queue against the rules engine's 71.2%.","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Results on the held-out set"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"In Billing & Payments the rules engine is more accurate: 84.7% against 83.7%.","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Results on the held-out set"},"summary":"Both statements are true of different segments. The classifier wins across all 4,800 held-out tickets and in four of five queues, and loses in Billing & Payments, where payment identifiers and card-decline phrasing match keyword rules exactly. A blanket 'replace the rules engine' framing drops the Billing exception; a Billing-first framing drops the overall result.","how_to_resolve":"Decide per queue rather than globally: specify whether Billing & Payments stays on rules while other queues move, and confirm the split holds outside the January–March held-out window, which the report flags as shaped by the post-holiday returns peak."},{"id":"C9","topic":"Which queue is the worst-routed — lowest accuracy vs largest share of misroutes","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"| Account & Access | 410 | 237 | 57.8% | 357 | 87.1% |","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, results table"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"Technical Faults routed to Orders & Delivery: 214 of 1,382 misroutes (15.5%)","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Misroute structure"},"summary":"Two defensible readings of 'the biggest routing problem'. By accuracy rate, Account & Access is worst (57.8%, on only 410 held-out tickets). By volume of misroutes, Technical Faults is worst, and it also carries the slowest resolution time of any queue (EV-dfe0bc2f: \"value: 34.1\", segment technical_faults, 2026-Q2). Each describes a different segment, and prioritising by rate and by volume point at different queues.","how_to_resolve":"State whether the team is optimising misroute rate or total misrouted tickets (and therefore total hours of delay), then rank queues on the chosen measure using 2026-Q2 volumes."},{"id":"C10","topic":"How costly a misroute is: 'agent moves it within the shift' vs 51.8-hour median","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-6404931e","quote":"Asked what happens today when a rule sends a ticket to the wrong place, she said the agent moves it, usually within the same shift.","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Ines Bracko"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8576e42f","quote":"value: 51.8","locator":"routing_metrics.csv row 15, period 2026-Q2, metric median_time_to_resolution_hours, segment misrouted"},"summary":"The Technical Faults team lead describes misroutes as cheap and quickly corrected; the metrics show reassigned tickets resolving in a median of 51.8 hours against 14.2 hours for tickets resolved in their first queue (EV-b7f6b080: \"value: 14.2\"). The gap cannot be attributed to misrouting alone — analytics notes there is no complexity score, so the two segments cannot be compared like for like.","how_to_resolve":"Measure the reassignment timestamp gap directly from routing_decision_log state transitions to test the 'same shift' claim, and note that per EV-3e2d12e8 there is \"no complexity or effort score on tickets\" to control for ticket difficulty."},{"id":"C11","topic":"Whether the classifier's cost is known","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-6404931e","quote":"The classifier will pay for itself inside a quarter.","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Tomas Ferreira"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"We have not estimated the cost of running or retraining this model in production.","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Limitations"},"summary":"A payback claim was made in the review; the trial team states no cost estimate exists, and the trial ran on unmetered shared batch capacity. The stakeholder record itself notes \"No cost model was presented and none exists.\"","how_to_resolve":"Require a serving-plus-retraining cost estimate on Modelyard and a stated benefit mechanism before treating payback as an input, given cost per ticket is a board-reported measure this year."},{"id":"C12","topic":"Vendor's 92% routing accuracy vs the in-house trial's 88.5%","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-6404931e","quote":"routes 92% of tickets correctly out of the box","locator":"stakeholder_notes.md, Vendor briefing (Tessarine AutoTriage)"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"Overall the classifier routed 88.5% of held-out tickets to the correct queue against the rules engine's 71.2%.","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Results on the held-out set"},"summary":"The two numbers are not measured on the same thing: the vendor figure has no stated sample, baseline, queue taxonomy or industry, while 88.5% is measured on 4,800 held-out Norvane tickets under the five-queue definition. They may both be accurate of different populations, and neither is evidence about the other. Separately, the vendor route faces governance friction: Tessarine \"would process ticket text on its own infrastructure\", while policy requires an assessment taking six to eight weeks.","how_to_resolve":"Ask Tessarine for the sample, taxonomy and baseline behind 92%, and confirm with legal-privacy whether in-region processing can be met at all before starting the data protection assessment, since EV-46e54a4b states \"Training or inference outside the region of origin is not permitted.\""},{"id":"C13","topic":"Manual triage desk: best measured accuracy vs frozen headcount","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-06ff9877","quote":"At that rate, covering every intake stream at current arrival volume would take about five full-time routers.","locator":"prior_experiments.md, Manual triage desk pilot"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-68cdd2b1","quote":"Support headcount is frozen for FY26.","locator":"support_objectives.md, Priorities and constraints"},"summary":"Hand routing produced the highest accuracy any intervention has shown (94.0% against 61.8% for the rules engine on comparable tickets), but scaling it needs about five FTEs against a frozen headcount and a flat cost-per-ticket goal. The pilot also covered one agent, one stream, two weeks, and says nothing about the other four queues.","how_to_resolve":"If the triage desk is to be considered, identify the offsetting reduction and get finance approval before a pilot, as the objectives require; otherwise record it as out of budget rather than out of evidence."},{"id":"C14","topic":"Whether any intervention has evidence on time-to-resolution, the actual decision metric","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-06ff9877","quote":"No intervention has been tested with time-to-resolution as its primary measure.","locator":"prior_experiments.md, Not attempted"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-8dc73255","quote":"Misroutes fall from 1,382 to 552, a reduction of 60.1%.","locator":"classifier_trial_report.md, Results on the held-out set"},"summary":"The decision question is about time-to-resolution, but the strongest available result is an offline routing-accuracy result. The trial states the link is not measured: \"Any statement about the effect on resolution time is an inference from the accuracy result, not a measurement of it.\" The one experiment that did measure resolution time, the intake form A/B, found 20.8 vs 21.1 hours and no meaningful difference.","how_to_resolve":"Run the shadow period the trial team recommends — classifier and rules engine both logged, rules applied — and measure accuracy and time-to-resolution on the same tickets, allowing for the 26-hour analytics lag before any read."}]}
